It's this time of the year that many graduating students are considering master's programs in the US and as I'm wrapping up my MPA at Columbia University, I thought I could share a few reflections In some parts of the world, like Europe and China, master's degree is something you do right after your bachelor's degree because it's accessible, affordable and a social norm.
I realised that in the US, this is really not the case for professional degrees – master's of public policy, business administration, education, environmental management and so on.
These programs are targeted at people who need them to get promoted on their current job or those who want to pivot to a new field.
While it's cool to meet mid-career professionals in your program (3-5 years of work experience), it also means that you will have to compete with them for summer internships and post-grad jobs.

author: Beniamin Strzelecki
text:
Post by Beniamin Strzelecki on 2026-04-05. 1 comments.
It's this time of the year that many graduating students are considering master's programs in the US and as I'm wrapping up my MPA at Columbia University, I thought I could share a few reflections In 
It's an uphill battle in an already tough job market that is unfriendly to international students (I made a post about it last year: https://www.facebook.com/groups/nyuad.room.of.requirement/posts/9587376384673563) Just to be clear – this has nothing to do with the quality of education that you are receiving.
I've learnt more than I expected and I love my program but I see from many of my classmates that your work experience pre-grad school is a huge determinant of where you can get after I'm a lot less familiar with degrees in humanities and arts, PhDs and other programs focused on further career in academia so others could speak about it.
There are also career paths where you really need that graduate degree, like law and medicine.
Lastly, if you got a good scholarship, it's probably still worth it to go for it because the chance might not repeat itself – which was the case for me.

The first half was nice, the concepts were pretty easy, just with much more rigorous proofs than in Intermediate Micro.
The second half was a bit more challenging, but still manageable.
Overall, I would say it was closer to math than econ, especially with formal notation and proofs, but there are a lot of applications in markets (mainly the same examples as in Micro though) The Professor is great, he has slides which help a lot, but sometimes I got lost in his explanations, especially in the second half of the course.

Post by Lovnish Julka on 2026-04-06. 5 comments.
Any reviews about Advanced Game Theory with Shuo Liu? How's the workload/ exams/ grading etc.
Exams were definitely easier than the problem sets, we had 2 midterms and an oral final (was supposed to be written), and the midterms had 3-4 questions each.
It was mainly theoretical questions + some computation to find an equilibrium or something, and knowing basic probability theory helps The Professor is lenient with grading, he definitely wants everybody to get a good grade, but you do have to put in effort to show that you understand the concepts.
We had 6-7 people left after add/drop, so I think he graded based on effort and understanding considering the oral final.
Overall, it's not an easy class for sure, but would recommend 100%

Comment by Sameer Kamran: Taking her sociological theory class with her currently.
Very very engaging class there’s tons of activities and art and the discussions are also very fun.
Shes also been one of the most accommodating professors in these times and even before this she would reaffirm her commitment to students’ mental health in class.

I took it with Pauline and while I think it’s not the best case scenario, it’s also not the worst.
The pros is that she teaches the very basics of economics so it’s good if you haven’t done any Econ before.
The cons are that she is very particular about what she wants from you.
She wants you to literally define every part of the question and explain every single equation you are using to the point of explaining what supply means and what demand means.
That being said, if you are able to study extra and adjust to her style, then u will be very able to get an A

text:
Post by Ab Alz on 2026-04-15. 7 comments.
Hi ! does anyone have the syllabus for Intro to Interactive Media with Prof M Ang, if so can you please share it with me + what are your thoughts about the class?
The class is pretty chill honestly and it’s kind of what you make of it.
Most assignments are quite simple, but it’s up to you to go above beyond or do the bare minimum and that can really change your experience.
Mang LOVES to talk and discuss (and can sometimes get carried away).
I wouldn’t say he’s the BEST professor, I definitely do still have plenty of doubts after every class but if you do put in the effort to personally ask him or go to his office hours, you’ll probably get your answers.
I found it a bit difficult to follow along with him in the first bit of the course (where we covered p5.js) because sometimes he wouldn’t really explain the code in the most ideal way.
Sometimes he would show code that has been written before, show us how it works and kind of roughly explain it.
I personally find it more helpful if he actually wrote the code live and explained as it he wrote (which he did do sometimes, but not always).

Post by Malika Singh on 2026-04-17. 9 comments.
Hello friends from Dhaka! I am here till the 26th of the month and looking to take away most I can from my time here. While all your recommendations in general are welcome I’m looking to learn about o
but in dhaka city itself, you can visit the dhaka university area, which is one of the oldest and most historically preserved areas.
go to TSC (imo one of best areas in dhaka to engage with student culture).
check out curzon hall, the DU library, and modhur canteen (a cafe/student meeting space where many student political movements started and it remains completely preserved and has not been modernised).
there's also bangla academy, shilpokola academy, drik, and nilkhet (literally an area with alleys crammed with ancient bookshops that are falling apart, but almost every book i read growing up was bought there).
visit icsba for archives on unpartitioned bengal, baatighor which is a small but beautiful library, and chhayanaut, which is the biggest cultural hub for music and the arts in dhaka.

you also must go to new market, you will never see such a mix of people from different social strata and economic backgrounds shopping together elsewhere.
try the small shingaras there, buy a saree from hawkers market, and visit noorjahan market and priyangon.
i think one of the peak shared moments of womanhood in dhaka is frantically hunting for fabric at priyangon for your next salwar kameez and hundreds of women also doing the same alongside you.
for souvenirs, you have to visit aarong.
dhakaiyas love to engage in cha and adda (tea and yapping).
grab a tong er cha (roadside tea) whenever you can, especially at TSC.
my favourite adda spots in dhaka are robindro shorobor (best motka malai cha in dhaka), the rooftop cafe at drik (i believe its called coffeegraphy), north end cafe, bengal boi (the shingara here with the green chutney is divine), jatra biroti.
you should also take a morning walk at ramna park.

All ages, all backgrounds, anyone over 18 who has something worth saying.

What we're looking for: Short, well-written pieces — 500 words maximum.
We're open to most formats: opinion, personal essay, cultural critique, short narrative, photography, illustration.
New pieces written specifically for this edition are preferred, but we're happy to consider pre-written work that fits the themes.

author: Jad Shatnawi
text:
Post by Jad Shatnawi on 2026-04-19. 1 comments.
[POSTING FOR A FRIEND] Hey everyone, We're looking for writers and journalists to contribute to a print newspaper being launched as part of a marketing campaign for a UAE-based brand. This is open to 
Some topics we'd love to see covered: — The art of slowing down // morning rituals, doing one thing at a time, being present — Dubai and UAE life // the expat experience, the city's quiet side, what home means to third culture kids — Food, drink, and sensory experience // taste, ritual, the difference between consuming and actually enjoying, favorite coffee shops, top food finds — Pop culture and celebrity // honest takes, sharp observations, things worth saying not just petty gossip — Arab artists and creatives // music, film, visual art, critique or profile of someone worth knowing — Local and regional commentary // culture, language, identity, what's changing and what isn't — Something educational but young // a concept, theory, or idea explained in a way your group chat would actually understand This list isn't exhaustive.
If you have a piece you're proud of or an idea that doesn't fit neatly into any of the above, pitch it anyway.

Comment by Udaya Pandit: A lot of people told me not to do that, so generally not advised, but it’s not entirely uncommon with bioengineers.
I did it and it was pretty stressful but turned out fine.
You just need to be really consistent in working for each class even before exams.
And get help from upperclassmen because resources will save u.
Don’t try to be a hero and do it all without help.
Every week, I had at least one and at most four quizzes on the same day.
So you will really have to study most weekends.
Plus hw and reports etc will never end.
The midterms weren’t at the same time (FoS was a week before LA) so they didn’t gang up until the final, where physics and LA were on the same day.
Smth like that will probably happen again, so keep that in mind.
It turned out fine because I did a lot of practice + got help from profs/recitation and upperclassmen/friends.
It was pressuring tho and I never want to do that again ✊ Hope this helps!

Hello everyone, My name is Mateja Damchevski, and I am a student researcher at NYU Abu Dhabi conducting an academic study that examines how a digital platform that connects residents with instructors for in-home swimming lessons can establish trust and demonstrate credibility.
This research is part of my undergraduate capstone project at NYU Abu Dhabi and is conducted under the supervision of Chinny Ogunro, Visiting Assistant Professor of Practice of Business, Organizations and Society at NYU Abu Dhabi.
The study has received institutional approval.
I am inviting the following groups to participate: • UAE residents who live in a community/building with an on-site swimming pool • Swimming instructors working anywhere in the UAE The survey takes around 15–20 minutes, and participation is voluntary.
Your data will remain confidential and mostly anonymized, and will be used strictly for academic research.

**The Library Presents: Stress Less Fest** Finals are here, so are we!
Join us virtually all next week for some stress less activities, hosted by the NYUAD Library.
**Pomodoro (Study with Me) ** Monday April 27 & Friday May 1, 5PM-7PM Sprint to the finish during our Pomodoro sessions on Monday and Friday!
The Pomodoro Technique is a time-management method designed to improve focus and productivity by breaking work into 25-minute intervals ("pomodoros") separated by 5-minute breaks.
Developed by Francesco Cirillo, it promotes deep work, reduces burnout, and manages distractions.
Drop in anytime and leave whenever you need.
**Library Office Hour Drop-In** Daily, 12 Noon-1PM Stuck on your research?
Struggling with citations?
Drop in and troubleshoot any final paper issues with a librarian.
No appointment needed.

Hi everyone, How’s CDAD-UH 1079 The Science of Making Music with Prof. Matteo Marciano and Prof. Andy Tillotson overall? Do you find the class worth taking and engaging, or do the quizzes (if there ar
[Disclaimer: I'm from a scientific/engineering background & LOVE music- hence, this was my BEST core] The class was very satisfying for someone curious about using both lenses to analyse music.
From one side, with Prof.
Andy (Completely different from his FoS version btw), we delved deep into the physics of sound, resonance, superposition..., and I admit that for someone with no prior physics/waves knowledge would have to put some effort to understand and solve the questions (It's not that type of core classes you just go into and start yapping/brainstorming).
On the other hand, the music production part with Prof.
Mateo was less demanding and more hands-on and fun.
Here, you'll enjoy the music more and put your physics knowledge to practise: from active listening to spectrum analysis, to basic mixing, all the way to synthesizing and composing.

# #NYUAnDHired 6: Summer Internship Grant Updates ## **STUDENT GOVERNMENT BITE — A SMALL UPDATE** **from:** Aymane, Student Government President **relevant team:** Executive Board Last year, StuGov received complaints from students who were rejected from grants.
Some students who were initially accepted later declined their awards, meaning that available funding could not always be redirected.
We are happy to announce that, thanks to CDC's work on the issue, their office intends to implement a waitlist system this year, so that if funding becomes available later, additional students may still have a chance to receive support.
This will allow more students to receive the grant.
Student Government followed up with CDC regarding the Summer Internship Grant disbursement timeline for Cycle 1 awardees, after students raised concerns that funds may only be disbursed in mid-May despite the award email indicating an approximate two-week timeline.

It is both a fun way to rate the songs and a research project on musical taste across cultures.
If you are into Eurovision, music, or just want to try something interesting, check it out below!
"Not sure how many of you follow Eurovision, but I know there are many Europeans in our community who might be quite into it.
I am pleased to share 12 Points, something I have been quietly working on for a while with collaborators at the University of Southern Denmark.
12 Points is a free app for rating every Eurovision entry, this year and in future editions.
You can browse the competing songs, record your reaction to each one, build a personal scorecard, share it with whoever needs to know your verdict, and see how your taste compares with others.
But it is also a research project.

Hi everyone! Sharing this on behalf of one of our NYUAD professors, who has been working on a free Eurovision rating app called 𝟏𝟐 𝐩𝐨𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐬. It is both a fun way to rate the songs and a research
Every rating will be anonymized, aggregated, and collected responsibly, following GDPR and research ethics guidelines.
It helps us study how musical taste varies across cultures and countries, and what individual preferences reveal when hundreds of thousands of them add up into a collective verdict.
Does the winner actually reflect what most people love?
Or does the way we make group decisions shape the outcome in ways we do not fully appreciate?
Eurovision is a great place to explore these sorts of questions and more.
If you are into music and especially Eurovision, you will enjoy it.
But if not, no worries.
You do not need to be a Eurovision fan to find the idea interesting.
You just need opinions about music, which I suspect most of you have.
Free, no ads, open to everyone everywhere.
The contest kicks off on May 12 and the Grand Final is on May 16 in Basel.
But you can join and start rating the songs right now.

text:
Post by Míra Schlotter on 2026-05-21. 1 comments.
Hello everyone, Quick course advert for Fall: "South Asia in the Indian Ocean World" (HIST-UH 1125X) with Professor Kulshreshtha - it's a history course, but also fills the X requirement. I took an art history course with the same professor, she was very understanding, gave constructive feedback and was always ready to help. Here is the course description: "The course offers an in‐depth study of the history and culture of the South Asians, who comprise the majority population of the United Arab Emirates. Situated at the center of the Indian Ocean world, the Indian subcontinent is currently home to over a billion people, and is the site of richly interconnected histories with regions around the wider Indian Ocean, including the Gulf. The course explores these histories, with a focus on understanding major cultural, political, economic, and social connections and changes as they affected ordinary people (including migrant laborers) and shaped the nature of collective identities (ethnic, national, religious, caste, class, gender, regional, and linguistic) over time. In developing an understanding of how collective identities were produced historically, students ultimately acquire valuable tools for appraising and navigating competing models of nationalism, cosmopolitanism, and universalism in the wider Indian Ocean world today."

Urgent: Need help reaching out to Global Ed Case 1: My Emirates ID expired in August 2025 while I was on my '1st' LOA (for Fall 2025).
And since, as a Bangladeshi, I would need a One-Time Entry Permit to enter the UAE again, I started mailing them periodically about it starting from mid October.
Three "we're looking into it"s later come January 12 2026, 6 days before my scheduled flight, I get an email from Ms.

To NYUAD graduates who are still living in Abu Dhabi, any advice on things to look out for while looking for places to rent in Reem/Masdar/Saadiyat, and what the typical price range would be, whether 
Utilities are usually not included unless the owner specifically mentions it (not common); some buildings that are owned by a sole owner and not landlords cover AC as part of the total rent but not water/electricity.
I would say always ask for a discount on total price because why not.
Take photos of any issues you see so you’re not responsibly for it later.
Check for any leaks and mold inside bathroom and kitchen cabinets.
If you can and if you know a building is owned by a single company or owner (meaning you don’t deal with private landlords but a developer or person who owns the whole building), try to go to the building reception you’re interested in directly or call the developers directly to ask if there are available units to avoid dealing with an agent and paying agency fees.
Saadiyat (NYUAD side) rent average these days are 70-85k for studio and 90-110k for a 1bd.
Other sides of Saadiyat are considerably higher.

Before you move in, you have a chance to point out any issues with the apartment and ask for those to be fixed: leak damage, mould in the AC ducts, drainage, water heater, leaky taps and bidet sprayers, wall paint.
Another big thing is improper rain insulation but that would be hard to check until the rainy season hits😬 Also - check the building that you want to rent on Google maps because tenants will sometimes leave a review pointing out major issues.

Also factor in an extra 5k+ into the rent shown on bayut for all the agency fees etc.

MALE PARTICIPANTS NEEDED FOR FMRI STUDY - UP TO 300 AED Here for the summer and curious about how your brain works?
Join our exciting research study and help us uncover how your brain processes memory!
The Sreenivasan Lab is recruiting participants for a psychology experiment regarding how certain activities may impact working memory.
We're using cutting-edge MRI technology to explore brain activity, and we need participants like you!
Eligibility requirements: You are eligible to participate if you are a male between 18 to 40 years old, right-handed, have normal or corrected to normal vision, are not colorblind, and do not have a history of brain injury, brain surgery or neurological condition.
Experiment details: The experiment may consist of two sessions.
Each session will last about 2.5 hours.

Guys, incoming freshman this side, a very random question as I went through the Albert Portal, why are majority of the classes only on Monday and Wednesday and can any upperclassmen (majoring in CS/Engineering) give me tips or advice on how to plan the classes to avoid burnout on these days ?
Comment by Hiyath Peiris: It’s very normal to have that pattern.
Monday-Wednesday and Tuesday-Thursday for lectures and Fridays for recitations/labs If you are undecided on CS or Engineering, pick Computer programing for engineers as it counts for both majors (you need to get an A- and above for it to could towards the CS degree requirements) Try to take a FWYS class and calculus.
These usually have a lot of sections so there’s ample room to pick a class that doesn’t fall back to back with your other classes.
For the remaining 4 credits, you could do a Core class or another CS/Eng requirement depending on how you want your schedule to be.

If you're undecided, I recommend taking CPE (A/A- in CPE counts for Intro to CS), Calc (or MVC, whatever you place into), FYWS, and a core in the first semester.
However, if, before course registration, you choose CS, you can replace the core with Discrete Mathematics.
It's a pre-req for other courses, so the faster you get done with it, the better.
And to avoid burnout, try to plan classes so that you have some break in between classes, especially for meals.
I had a horrible meal schedule the first semester since I had 3 classes continuously from 9:55 to 2:00, so my first meal of the day was at 2:30 PM.
Avoid that at any cost.
Keep in track with your classes from the very beginning, and you'll be fine!

I'm Shinyi, Class of 22/23 alum, now based in Zurich, Switzerland 🙂 We are looking for participants for an interview study on how people use digital technologies in their everyday lives. **All adult digital users are welcome**! * Who can participate?: **Adults aged 18 or older** who use a smartphone, tablet, or computer at least four days per week. Must be able to participate in the interview in English. * What does participation involve?: A one-on-one interview lasting between 30 and 75 minutes, conducted via video call or in-person. The interview will ask about your everyday digital routines and how you use digital tools and platforms. The interview will be audio-recorded. * Compensation: Participants will receive compensation equivalent to** 50 US Dollars **(approximately 40 CHF / 184 AED) in the form of vouchers or direct payment upon completion. Interested? Please complete a brief pre-screening survey here (https://forms.cloud.microsoft/e/4UHYtHbA3B). For questions, contact me at shinyi.kang@uzh.ch. Hello, I'm a rising sophomore in CS and could use some advice on planning out my sophomore year.
Last spring I took Data Structures and Discrete, and taking them together with a FYWS was challenging.
Then, I did Multivariable Calc over the summer which was also rough lol.
So, this year I really want a balanced schedule instead of dumping all the hard courses into one semester.
I'm thinking of spreading LA, CSO, CN, and Algo across the year, since CSO and Algo are prereqs for the second study away and I want them done in time.
My plan is to keep fall lighter, just one of these four plus some gen electives and core requirements, and then take the rest of the challenging courses in spring, since I'm planning to study away in Paris that semester.
Does that sound like a reasonable way to balance things out?
And if you've taken these, which one would you start with in the fall?

Hello!
I hope you are well.
My name is Pamela Martinez and a NYUAD 2023 Alumni.
I am reaching out to you to ask for support.
You may have heard, there were two earthquakes back-to-back in Venezuela, leaving thousands of people under the rubble and many survivors who have lost their homes.
Civilians are mobilizing and organizing to rescue people with the resources they have at hand, and to distribute health supplies, clothes, and food in the most affected areas.
If you’re in a position to help, there are two ways to support: 1.⁠ ⁠URGENT RESPONSE: I have a group of trusted friends who are delivering machinery and equipment for people attempting to rescue people under the rubble.
It’s all civilians on the ground but trusted people I love.
We are doing this as a response of lack of governmental and state response.
We have bought so far electric hammers, grinders, rescue kits, and other tools that cut through dense materials.

author: Parth Sanjay Badgujar
text:
Post by Parth Sanjay Badgujar on 2026-07-16. 7 comments.
HI Guys **Looking for experiences in CPE hows the course like and what advice would you guys give to score A or higher **
I’d advise you to choose as simple a project as possible and execute it well using the material you’ve learnt in class rather than trying something insanely complicated.
The mentors you will be assigned will be useless by design (as in previous years there were cases of them doing a lot of the team’s work) so I would recommend reaching out to lab instructors, TAs, the prof, Reddit, really anywhere you can in case you’re stuck (even ROR!) The assignments are pretty tricky.
In the fall sem they made it so AI wouldn’t work on the assignments (like our 2nd one was on trajectories which was notoriously hard for models at the time).
Do NOT try to leave it to 1-2 days before the deadline, they take a lot of brainstorming and research, sometimes asking your friends.
I’d really really recommend sitting down with the TAs if you’re really struggling to crack an aspect of the assignment or you have 0 idea where to begin, that’s what I did (shoutout to my lovely TAs) and it helped me out a lot in coming up with a plan.

author: Parth Sanjay Badgujar
text:
Post by Parth Sanjay Badgujar on 2026-07-16. 7 comments.
HI Guys **Looking for experiences in CPE hows the course like and what advice would you guys give to score A or higher **
Our first two assignments were basic C++, third one was OOP focused and last one was MATLAB.
The assignments typically consist of a report that holds way more marks for showing your research, your logic (algorithm), input/output diagrams, test cases.
Make sure you give all of these a lot of time and attention as they constitute a big chunk of the grade.
My code was faulty in some cases and I still got an okay grade because my reports made sense.
As for research, which you will absolutely need bcs some of the things asked won’t be in syllabus and will require creativity and you looking for answers (especially for team project!) the professors want you to show where you got your info from, so credit everything you use and try not to get all your information from AI.
And if you do use AI, make sure you credit its use because the prof might question you if they see your assignment code uses knowledge you weren’t taught in class or the textbook.

Comment by Saher Khaled: So to get a driving license in abu dhabi You need first to do an eye exam/test then open a traffic file through tamm Then you need to go to EDC (emirates driving company) and register for theoretical classes (online classes) Then register for a theory exam at EDC Once you pass(36/45 is the passing grade if I remember correctly) Then you can sign up for driving school classes inside the EDC (The cheapest option is 16 classes in 16 days and you can take it in less time but more expensive) After you finish EDC classes (in person) you do a parking test inside the school (parallel parking and 90-degree parking) After you pass the test you apply for a training license through Tamm Then youcan sign up for driving classes with an external instructor (driving in Abu Dhabi) you need minimum 6 hours After that the instructor will issue you a training certificate then you can apply for the police driving test Once you do it and pass the test you can apply for your driving license in Tamm Keep in mind that this process

Philosophy and Physics at the Intersection Hi RoR!
Professor Kevin Coffey will be teaching “PHIL-UH 2910: Philosophical Puzzles at the Atomic Scale: Measurement, Chance, and Spooky Action at a Distance” (Previously titled: Philosophy of Quantum Mechanics) next semester.
If you’re interested not only in quantum mechanics but also in the different ways of interpreting what quantum mechanics tells us about reality, I’d highly recommend taking a look at this course.
It’s a rare opportunity to explore questions at the intersection of physics and philosophy — questions about measurement, probability, reality, and the nature of the physical world.

author: Allen Kurban
text:
Post by Allen Kurban on 2026-07-24. 9 comments.
Philosophy and Physics at the Intersection Hi RoR! Professor Kevin Coffey will be teaching “PHIL-UH 2910: Philosophical Puzzles at the Atomic Scale: Measurement, Chance, and Spooky Action at a Distanc
The course also counts toward the Math major, so it’s a great way to satisfy a requirement while trying something outside the usual mathematics curriculum I am copying the course description by the professor below: ‘The legendary physicist Richard Feynman wrote in his Lectures on Physics that “[a]lthough it is interesting and worth while to study the physical laws simply because they help us to understand and to use nature, one ought to stop every once in a while and think, ‘What do they really mean?’”.
This course is an attempt to do just that for the physical laws governing the quantum domain.
We know that the world they describe is profoundly weird, but it turns out that there are radically different and incompatible ways of making sense of that weirdness—ways that are grounded as much in philosophical and conceptual considerations as they are in experimental data.
postPreview: Philosophy and Physics at the Intersection Hi RoR! Professor Kevin Coffey will be teaching “PHIL-UH 2910: Philosophical Puzzles at the Atomic Scale: Measurement

author: Allen Kurban
text:
Post by Allen Kurban on 2026-07-24. 9 comments.
Philosophy and Physics at the Intersection Hi RoR! Professor Kevin Coffey will be teaching “PHIL-UH 2910: Philosophical Puzzles at the Atomic Scale: Measurement, Chance, and Spooky Action at a Distanc
For example, what does it mean for a particle to be in a superposition?
We know how to represent such a state mathematically, but how ought we to conceptualize the part of the physical world to which that mathematics corresponds?
Does the quantum world really entail ‘spooky action at a distance’, as some have thought, so that what happens in one region of space could instantaneously affect some other region in a distant galaxy?
(If so, how is that consistent with relativity?
How could the scientific project even be possible in such a world?) Is our best theory of the quantum regime ultimately a theory about observers or minds or measurements or consciousness or q-bits of information, and so not really a theory of an independently-existing objective physical world at all?
And does chance or indeterminism play a fundamental role at the quantum level, or is it merely a reflection of our own ignorance?

author: Allen Kurban
text:
Post by Allen Kurban on 2026-07-24. 9 comments.
Philosophy and Physics at the Intersection Hi RoR! Professor Kevin Coffey will be teaching “PHIL-UH 2910: Philosophical Puzzles at the Atomic Scale: Measurement, Chance, and Spooky Action at a Distanc
If it plays a fundamental role, how do we explain why things happen as they do?
As we’ll see, different ways of understanding the laws of quantum mechanics answer all of these questions in strikingly different ways.
Not for nothing did Feynman also once say: “I think I can safely say that nobody understands quantum mechanics”!
This is not a course in the physics of quantum theory, but a course in the philosophy of quantum theory.
Although we will (of course) have to learn the basic structure of quantum mechanics along the way, no specific knowledge of physics or philosophy is presupposed and there will be no problem sets.
Rather, once we’ve discussed the core principles of the theory, our aim will be to think carefully about the main concepts and investigate ways of conceptualizing how the whole structure fits together.

Comment by Oscar Wang: Yes, I tried it last weekend. The station in Abu Dhabi is quite far (in Musaffah) from the center but parking is free. The trains are nice and on-time, it will only take you 1h45min to go from FUJ to AUH. Apart from the station location and current frequency of trains, I could not find any down sides as a quite experienced train traveler around the world and enthusiast for public transport. I would recommend it for commuting if your company is close to the station / any ER shuttle or city bus shuttle stations. Another concern would be that after opening of new stations later this year, the schedule might be more packed given that it is a mostly single-track, freight-prioritized line. Also, there may be additional stops for AUH-FUJ services, increasing the travel time.

author: Maha Rashid
text:
Post by Maha Rashid on 2026-08-05. 0 comments.
For anyone looking for fun classes this fall: I'm helping Professor Vikram spread the word about two courses with open spots. **WALLS: Cultural Witness, Social Catalyst** asks you to revisit a wall you've known intimately, be it from home, a neighborhood, or somewhere personal, and use it as a departure point for artistic inquiry. You'll research the aesthetic, historic, and anthropological layers of an everyday wall, then return to the studio to create work across a range of mediums. This is a graduate course but is open to undergrads too! **City to Studio: Transforming Urban Research** treats Abu Dhabi itself as the studio. Through extensive field research around the city, you'll create artworks that stake a claim on public space and examine how artists can embed their questions into the social fabric of a place. Both courses are highly research driven and push you to think about the built environment as material for art. Would recommend if you have room in your schedule! **WALLS: Cultural Witness, Social Catalyst (ARTMD-GH 5133)** Thursdays, 8:30 am -12:30 pm **City to Studio: Transforming Urban Research (CADT-UH 1097)** Tuesdays 3:20 - 4:35 pm & Thursdays 3:20 - 6:00 pm.

# **[Advice needed from locals]** **Hi guys, I am both a chef and a horseback archery enthusiast. Since I heard that the UAE, along with other Gulf countries, has a pretty rich cultural history regard
Waitrose is more expensive, Spinneys is okay, but both don’t have a good ordering system, so you get their stuff from Talabat/Deliveroo or drive yourself.
For Korean (and some Japanese) food/ingredients, you have 1004 Mart.
For Japanese, it’s likely Deans Fujiya, but orders can take a bit of time to get to you.
Wemart has really good veggies, bread, and Chinese food/ingredients, also very affordable.
There is also a fish market in Mina port and Fruit and Vegetable Souq here.
In terms of cooking equipment, I either used to buy from Amazon or ship it myself through package forwarding from overseas.
Locally, some brands either aren’t available in stores (like Madein / Nordicware, etc.) or are overpriced to the point of you buying it abroad and shipping it here being cheaper.
If electronic, make sure it matches the local voltage and outlets.
Also, some cooking ingredients you can also get from Amazon.

Hi ROR, Has anyone ever tried to build a better way to search through old ROR posts?
Facebook group search is pretty bad.
A lot of the time, someone's already asked the exact question you have and gotten useful answers, but you can’t find the old post, so you end up making another post asking the same thing.
Since I feel like a lot of the questions posted here have already been asked and answered before.
The problem tends to be finding those old posts.
I was thinking it could be useful to build a simple ROR-specific search tool where you could ask something like: “Has anyone had trouble getting X from Y department?” It would pull up relevant posts and comments, summarize what people suggested, link back to the original threads, and maybe show who dealt with the same issue in case you wanted to reach out.
It would basically be a way to make the years of useful information on ROR actually searchable instead of buried in Facebook.

## [Church Shuttle Guide] Hello all, welcome back to a start of a new semester! For those that would be interested in going to church, this is a quick announcement regarding shuttles provided by the school for international churches in Abu Dhabi. The shuttle for **Grace Church** will depart at *3:45 PM* every Saturday from the Welcome Center (in front of A4, East Administration Building). The shuttle for **ECC (Evangelical Community Church)** and/or **St. Andrew's Church** will depart at *9:15 AM* every Sunday from behind D1. There are also other churches with differing timings such as the Korean Onnuri church (with shuttle transportation) and churches without dedicated transportation, so if you would like more information, we'd be happy to connect you to the right people and resources. There will also be Bible Study every week hosted by the Mustard Seed Subcommittee and other events but more information will be shared later regarding this! If you have any questions, feel free to reach out either to Sheena Chiang, Nelson Mbigili, or me. Safe travels back to campus everybody!

Hi everyone !
I’m currently developing my Film & New Media capstone, and I’m looking to speak with 5–10 neurodivergent people from the NYUAD community or outside over the next 2-3 weeks.
I’d really love to hear from people with different experiences and perspectives.
The film is exploring neurodivergence as a diverse range of ways of experiencing the world, and how much of the difficulty people face can come from environments and systems that aren't built to accommodate different ways of thinking, communicating, learning, or just living life.
The project will be a patchwork of fiction and documentary.
I’ll be interviewing people about their own experiences, and these conversations will help inform and inspire fictional scenes in the film.
So I’m not trying to make a documentary that simply explains what neurodivergence is , but instead I want the real experiences of different people to actually shape a fictional short film.

Hi everyone ! I’m currently developing my Film & New Media capstone, and I’m looking to speak with 5–10 neurodivergent people from the NYUAD community or outside over the next 2-3 weeks. I’d really lo
I’m interested in hearing from people who: have a formal diagnosis or are currently in the process of seeking a diagnosis or feel that they may be neurodivergent but haven't pursued or received a formal diagnosis.
There’s absolutely no expectation that you need to have everything figured out or identify with a particular label.
Your own experience is what I’m interested in.
Ideally, I’d love to interview people on camera, but if you’d rather not be filmed, I’m also very happy to do an audio-only/off-camera interview.
We can talk beforehand about what you’re comfortable sharing.
One important thing to be transparent about: the documentary interviews/material themselves may or may not appear in the final film.
That is something I want to leave open and let the filmmaking process determine.

Hi everyone ! I’m currently developing my Film & New Media capstone, and I’m looking to speak with 5–10 neurodivergent people from the NYUAD community or outside over the next 2-3 weeks. I’d really lo
The main purpose of these conversations is to learn from people's experiences and use them as creative material to develop the fictional parts of the project.
If documentary footage or audio does end up being used in the final film, that would be discussed with you as part of the process.
The interviews would be relatively informal and more of a conversation than sg formal.
It can be shorter or longer, we can do it in your room, in front library , over a lunch or coffee , or whatever works the best.
I’m especially interested in the little everyday things: how you study, work, communicate, organise your space, deal with sensory experiences, what helps you function, what people misunderstand about you, or moments where a small accommodation made a big difference.
But at the end of the day I just want to listen to your stories.
If you’re interested, or even just curious and want to hear more, please DM me!

**PARTICIPANTS NEEDED FOR A PSYCHOLOGY STUDY** **Earn up to 450 AED in Gratitude Vouchers (e.g., Amazon gift cards)!** Hi, everyone! The Sreenivasan Lab is conducting a research study for a project examining how hormones influence memory across the menstrual cycle. We are looking for female participants with regular cycles who are interested in contributing to research in women's health. **What you’ll be asked to do:** * Fill out a form that will ask questions to determine initial eligibility * If eligible based on the questions, provide a blood sample for genetic testing (COMT gene) * If you meet the genetic criteria, track your menstrual cycle using an app (Euki) and at-home LH urine-based test strips * If eligible based on cycle tracking, complete two memory experiments (each ~90 minutes), scheduled during different hormonal phases of your cycl * Submit two venous blood samples for hormone analysis (estrogen, progesterone, LH) Participants must be available to attend both required experimental sessions in-person. Eligibility requirements will be shared via email with interested participants. We will ask for minimal information to determine your eligibility in the initial survey and will avoid collecting any details we do not need. ## ## TLDR: Joint documentary film being made across India-Pakistan.
Requesting you to come forward and fund it in whatever capacity you can.
Please?
Hi folks, here’s a documentary project that Ibad Hassan and I have been working on since December.
**https://seermeinmanikmotilal.com/ ** **^**find here the **trailer, photographs, and a published report **for The Polis Project that we authored a few months ago The film is a story of **fisherfolk families who often get detained** near a disputed region between the ever-hostile states of India and Pakistan.
From fishing villages of Karachi to the settlements of southern Gujarat, we want to explore a shared reality from both sides; of navigating day-to-day lives in the absence of loved ones, fishing in dying coasts, and fishermen seeking long voyages in the Arabian Sea despite endless risk.

posting on behalf of a friend, emirati women participants needed for research!!!🙏 Hello! I'm an NYUAD psychology student conducting a research study on how family emotional environments shape emotion regulation and coping in young Emirati women. If you're an Emirati woman aged 18–25 and currently enrolled at NYUAD, you're warmly invited to participate. It's an online survey and takes about 15–25 minutes with a raffle entry upon completion. This opportunity is ideal for candidates who are considering graduate school studies, publications, or research-related careers in the social sciences. ❌ There’s a common MYTH that eating eggs or meat every day is automatically bad for your health and will raise your cholesterol But it’s not that simple. The important thing is not just whether you eat eggs or meat, but how much saturated fat you consume throughout the entire day 👆🏻 A high intake of saturated fat can contribute to higher LDL (“bad”) cholesterol. But if you have eggs for breakfast and then choose mostly unsaturated fats for the rest of the day — such as olive oil, nuts, avocado and other plant-based sources — you can still have a healthy, balanced diet ✅ Personally, I eat eggs every morning and simply pay attention to the overall balance of my diet. 👉 Don’t blame one food. Look at the whole picture. It’s your overall daily diet that matters, not the fact that you ate a few eggs. #diet #health #healthyfood #fatloss

Fallen Icarus At The Temple Of Concordia 🔍 HD version: https://www.360cities.net/image/fallen-icarus-at-the-temple-of-concordia The Temple of Concordia stands in the Valley of the Temples at Agrigento, Sicily, on the site of the ancient Greek city of Akragas. Built around 440–430 BC, it is one of the finest and best-preserved examples of Doric architecture. Its exceptional state of preservation is partly due to its conversion into a Christian church in late antiquity. In front of the temple lies Icaro Caduto (Fallen Icarus), a monumental bronze sculpture by Polish artist Igor Mitoraj, donated to the archaeological park in 2011. Inspired by the Greek myth of Icarus, the fallen figure creates a striking contrast between contemporary sculpture and the monumental architecture of the ancient world.
